FangRidderXie2026: fixed-positive-penalty efficient DR optimizer limit; BelloniChernozhukovChetverikovWei2018: generic uniform architecture.

soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-interior
soundness_flags.one_line: Its FangRidderXie2026 citation supplies interiority for one fixed penalty, not a uniform positive distance over the proposed interval of c values.

soundness_flags.label: ass:smooth-criterion
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited anchor assumes twice differentiability/local smoothness for a fixed penalty and its Condition (S) controls two theta derivatives; it does not support the stated three-theta-derivative, uniform-in-c condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:uniform-curvature
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited anchor requires a positive-definite Hessian at one fixed optimizer, not the displayed infimum-over-c curvature lower bound.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: oeq:foldwise-replacement and Theorems 1–4
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The uniform empirical replacement radius delta_n=o_P(1) remains the stated unresolved proof target.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The joint frontier law, multiplier validity, tube, and regret calibration are conditional on establishing this explicit replacement result.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, Assumption 3, lines 209–221; Appendix B Condition (S), lines 779–788
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Assumption 3 imposes compactness, a unique interior optimizer, twice differentiability, and positive-definite Hessian for a fixed lambda; Condition (S) bounds only first and second theta derivatives. It does not state uniform-in-lambda/c interiority, three derivatives, or a uniform curvature lower bound.
Theorem 2 gives the fixed-penalty Hessian-quadratic regret limit and Theorem 5 gives the efficient cross-fitted doubly robust optimizer and regret limits.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and manuscript Sections 2–3; reporting-guarantee discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The manuscript develops risk-aware policy selection using Gaussian-bootstrap critical values and supplies reporting guarantees for the selected policy.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Retag the three genuinely stronger path-uniform regularity conditions as novel with a concrete analytic justification, or replace the Fang citation by a source proving the required compact-index uniform M-estimation conditions.

Make the field contribution sharper by proving a finite-sample or explicit rate for delta_n in terms of the two nuisance rates and the softmax feature/curvature constants, rather than leaving the central novelty as an o_P(1) verification.

Add a strict comparison showing when the shared-frontier procedure improves on a named pointwise-reporting workflow, for example simultaneous familywise coverage or a strictly smaller calibrated post-selection loss bound than separately Bonferroni-calibrated fixed-c intervals.

recommended_next_step: Revise the unsupported standard tags and strengthen the replacement theorem into an explicit quantitative frontier advance; then continue this field-level angle.
